newsitem.title: JAPAN: INTERVIEW--Naigai Clothes aims for TSE listing.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW--Naigai Clothes aims for TSE listing.

text.p: Naigai Clothes Co Ltd expects to post a 10 percent rise in sales for the year to March 31, 1998, and eventually aims to list its shares on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange (TSE) president Yasutaka Nishizaki said on Tuesday.

"We previously announced that our 1997/98 parent sales would grow 7.2 percent from the previous year, but we now think that we will be able to achieve a gain of about 10 percent," he told Reuters in an interview.
"After our business results for 1997/98 become available, we would like to apply as early as 1998/99 for a share listing on the TSE," he said.
"We expect the (TSE) listing to provide us with more business opportunities and to boost morale among our employees," he added.
The Osaka-based apparel manufacturer is currently listed on the second section of the Osaka Securities Exchange.
In May, Naigai Clothes announced that it expected to post a parent current profit of 1.80 billion yen on sales of 43 billion yen in 1997/98.
"We eventually aim for an improvement in profitability rather than an increase in sales, but for the time being, we hope to boost sales a little more," Nishizaki said.
In 1996/97, sales and profits rose for a third consecutive business year, with parent current profit up 38.7 percent at 1.46 billion yen and sales up 13.4 percent at 40.08 billion yen.
The 13.4 percent increase in sales was the largest among the 32 major Japanese apparel makers, Nishizaki said.
"There is much potential for growth," he added.

More than half of Naigai's revenue comes from sales of underwear and sleepwear, items which consumers need to replace periodically, so the company benefits from demand for its products regardless of the state of the Japanese economy, he said.
